featureRef: 4.5 Recording a payment and issuing the receipt
name: Record money received against the right invoice, by whichever route it arrived, and issue the receipt
priorityReason: Every rupee the school takes passes through here. It is the single point where money meets the ledger.

goal.capability: to record a payment against the right invoice however it arrived, and give the payer proof
goal.outcome: the family's balance and the school's books agree, and the payer holds a numbered receipt

postConditions: The payment is recorded against the invoice it was for, and the invoice reads Paid or Partially paid accordingly.
A numbered receipt exists and has been issued to the guardian, so the payer holds proof of what they paid.
The entry has posted to the student ledger and to the general ledger, so the family's balance and the school's books agree.
The route the money arrived by is recorded — online, bank or cash — which is what reconciliation reads afterwards.
The invoice has left overdue tracking where it is now settled.
A payment recorded in error is corrected through its own use case, never by editing this entry.
No payment exists without a receipt, and no receipt exists without a ledger posting. The three are created together or not at all.

businessRules.rule: A payment is always recorded against an invoice. Money received without an invoice to apply it to is held as an unallocated receipt and reported, not absorbed.
All three routes — online, bank challan and cash at the counter — are recorded here as a payment. The route is held on the record, because reconciliation reads it afterwards.
A bank payment is entered from the stamped school copy, matched by its challan reference. Without a matching reference no payment is recorded, because a guess would credit the wrong family.
The payment date is when the money was received, not when it was keyed. A challan paid on Friday and entered on Monday is dated Friday, or the day's collection figure is wrong.
A part payment is permitted. The invoice reads Partially paid and the balance stays outstanding.
A payment may not exceed the invoice's outstanding balance. An overpayment is refused rather than creating a negative balance.
Receipt numbers are gapless per branch and academic session and are never reused. A failed entry consumes no number.
An online payment confirmed by the gateway is recorded automatically, with no keying. The gateway's transaction reference is held against it.
Payment, receipt and ledger postings are created together or not at all. A payment with no receipt, or a receipt with no posting, is the failure this rule exists to prevent.
A recorded payment is never edited. A wrongly recorded payment is corrected through its own use case, which reverses the entry and records a new one with a reason.
The receipt is issued to the guardian at the point of recording, so the payer holds proof without asking for it.
Recording a payment removes the invoice from overdue tracking where it is now settled, and stops any further late fee accruing on it.

basicFlow.navigation: Pays online, at the bank, or in cash at the office counter
basicFlow.userAction: Pays the fee by one of the three routes.
Finds the invoice directly, or by the challan reference on the stamped school copy.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Resolves the reference to an invoice and shows its outstanding balance. Refuses a reference that does not match.

basicFlow.navigation: Record payment → Route, amount and date
basicFlow.userAction: Selects the route, enters the amount received and the date the money arrived.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the amount is above zero and not more than the outstanding balance, and that the date is when the money was received.

basicFlow.navigation: Record payment → Record and issue receipt
basicFlow.systemResponse: Creates the payment, generates the numbered receipt and posts to both ledgers, together or not at all.
Issues the receipt to the guardian, so the payer holds proof without asking for it.
Moves the invoice to Paid or Partially paid, and removes it from overdue tracking where it is settled.
Posts the credit to the student ledger and the double entry to the general ledger, so the family's balance and the school's books agree.

alternateFlows.condition: The family pays online through the gateway
alternateFlows.behaviour: The confirmation records the payment automatically, with no keying, and holds the gateway's transaction reference against it (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The family returns a stamped school copy of a challan
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Fee → Record payment → Challan reference
alternateFlows.behaviour: The reference on the stamped copy resolves to the invoice, and the payment is entered from it with the bank's stamp date (BR-3, BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The family pays less than the full amount
alternateFlows.behaviour: The part payment is recorded, the invoice reads Partially paid and the balance stays outstanding (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: Money arrives with no invoice to apply it to
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is held as an unallocated receipt and reported, rather than being absorbed into an invoice it was not for (BR-1).

alternateFlows.condition: A payment was recorded against the wrong student
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Fee → Receipt log → Correct payment
alternateFlows.behaviour: The entry is reversed and a new one recorded with a reason. The original is never edited (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian asks for the receipt again
alternateFlows.behaviour: The same numbered receipt is reproduced, not a new one, so one payment never carries two receipt numbers (BR-7).

exceptions.condition: The challan reference does not match any challan
exceptions.systemResponse: No payment is recorded against a guess (BR-3).
exceptions.messageShown: No challan matches that reference. Check the stamped copy.

exceptions.condition: The invoice has already been paid in full
exceptions.messageShown: This invoice was settled on 08-09-2026 by receipt RCP/LHR/26-27/002218.

exceptions.condition: The amount is greater than the outstanding balance
exceptions.systemResponse: The payment is refused rather than creating a negative balance (BR-6).
exceptions.messageShown: The outstanding balance is PKR 4,000. Enter that or less.

exceptions.condition: The amount is zero or negative
exceptions.messageShown: Enter an amount greater than zero.

exceptions.condition: The payment date is in the future
exceptions.messageShown: The payment date cannot be in the future.

exceptions.systemResponse: The whole entry is rolled back. No payment, no receipt and no posting exist, and no receipt number is consumed (BR-7, BR-9).
exceptions.messageShown: The payment could not be recorded. Nothing has been saved.

exceptions.condition: An online confirmation arrives twice for the same transaction
exceptions.systemResponse: The second is recognised by its gateway reference and recorded once (BR-8).
exceptions.messageShown: This payment has already been recorded under receipt RCP/LHR/26-27/002218.

exceptions.condition: Accounts attempt to edit a recorded payment
exceptions.messageShown: A recorded payment cannot be edited. Use Correct payment, which needs School Admin approval.

exceptions.condition: The receipt message to the guardian fails
exceptions.systemResponse: The payment and the receipt stand and the send is marked Failed. It can be resent.
exceptions.messageShown: The payment is recorded. The receipt could not be sent — resend it from the receipt log.

departures.requirement: A cash payment is recorded and its receipt printed within 5 seconds, since a queue forms at the counter on fee days.
Payment, receipt and both ledger postings commit together. A payment with no receipt, or a receipt with no posting, must never exist.
Receipt numbers stay gapless under concurrent entry at several counters, and a failed entry consumes none.
Payments, receipts and their postings are retained 7 years as financial records and are never hard-deleted.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
